dimensions.name: 21st Century Skills & AI Literacy
dimensions.objective: Increase the number and skills of AI talent and prepare the workforce for changing skills demand.
dimensions.rationale: Nothing else in the framework moves without people who can build, buy and govern AI. Skills is the slowest-moving enabler and the one with the longest lag to impact.

dimensions.name: Reliable Infrastructure & Compute Capacity
dimensions.objective: Increase access to scalable storage and high-performance computing infrastructure.
dimensions.rationale: Connectivity, electricity, data centres and accelerated compute set the ceiling on what can be built and served locally.

dimensions.name: Robust Data Strategy
dimensions.objective: Increase availability of and access to quality data for training AI models through data-sharing frameworks and guidance.
dimensions.rationale: Models are trained on data. Without Rwandan datasets, Rwandan problems get solved with other countries' data or not at all.

dimensions.name: Trustworthy AI Adoption in the Public Sector
dimensions.objective: Accelerate public sector AI adoption to improve services and lead by example with lighthouse projects.
dimensions.rationale: Government is the largest single buyer and the most visible adopter. Public deployments set norms for everyone else.

dimensions.name: Widely Beneficial AI Adoption in the Private Sector
dimensions.objective: Boost productivity in key sectors, scale adoption from start-ups to corporates, increase AI employment.
dimensions.rationale: This is where the economic value in the 2022 sizing study would actually be captured.

dimensions.name: Practical AI Ethical Guidelines
dimensions.objective: Mitigate AI risks, promote responsible adoption, uphold national priorities in privacy, security and ethics.
dimensions.rationale: Adoption without safeguards is fragile. Ethics instruments are also preconditions for scoring in the global indices.
